children.title: Trump threatens jail for reporter who would not identify Iran rescue source
children.description_medium: At an April 6, 2026 White House press conference, Trump said the news organization that first reported the rescue of a downed U.S. airman in Iran should identify its source and that the reporter could go to jail for refusing. The remark addressed a demand for disclosure of a journalistic source.
children.description_long: At a White House press conference on April 6, 2026, Trump addressed reporting about the rescue of a downed U.S. airman in Iran. He said the news organization that first reported the rescue should identify its source and said the reporter could go to jail for refusing. Reuters reported the remarks as a public threat directed at the reporter’s refusal to reveal a source. The statement concerned a specific report about the rescue and a demand that the news organization identify its source. The supplied report supports the date, setting, subject of the coverage, and substance of Trump’s comments. It does not establish that a reporter was subsequently jailed, that the government formally compelled disclosure in this episode, or that this remark initiated the later grand-jury subpoenas discussed in separate reporting. The public statement is therefore recorded as its own event. The packet provides no evidence establishing a causal link between this April comment and the Justice Department’s later subpoenas to other reporters.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the press conference date reported by Reuters.

children.title: DOJ withdraws subpoenas to Post and Journal reporters
children.description_medium: In June 2026, the Justice Department issued and later withdrew grand-jury testimony subpoenas to one Washington Post reporter and three Wall Street Journal reporters in national-security leak investigations. Public reporting said the investigations’ precise subjects and scope were unclear. The article did not establish their exact targets.
children.description_long: The Justice Department issued grand-jury subpoenas seeking testimony from one Washington Post reporter and three Wall Street Journal reporters in national-security leak investigations, then withdrew the subpoenas. The Washington Post reported the developments on June 23, 2026. Its account said the precise subjects and scope of the investigations were unclear. The supplied evidence thus supports the number and affiliations of the reporters, the fact that the subpoenas sought grand-jury testimony, their subsequent withdrawal, and the uncertainty about what the investigations concerned. The subpoenas are distinct from Trump’s April 6 public threat to jail a reporter who would not identify a source for reporting about an Iran airman rescue. Available reporting in this packet does not establish that these subpoenas concerned that disclosure or resulted from Trump’s comments. The record does not supply exact dates for the issuance and withdrawal, so June 23 is treated as the article’s publication date rather than an asserted date for both legal steps.
children.date_uncertainty: June 23, 2026 is the Washington Post publication date; the supplied packet does not give exact issuance or withdrawal dates.

unresolved_components.title: Connection between Iran airman-rescue report and reporter subpoenas
unresolved_components.reason: The packet says the subpoenas’ precise subjects were unclear.
unresolved_components.missing_evidence: Evidence identifying the subpoenas’ investigation scope and showing they concerned the airman-rescue disclosure.

rationale: The supplied sources support two separate events but do not connect the later subpoenas to the airman-rescue report. The descriptions distinguish reported facts from unresolved investigation scope.
